clue.text: Fancy Prussia suppressing a republic

indicators.note: suppressing means keeping something down out of sight, so the answer lies concealed inside these two words

explanation.surface: An image of Prussia, fancied up, crushing some smaller republic beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' tells you the letters are held down inside 'Fancy Prussia', running from the end of the first word into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island nation in the eastern Mediterranean governed as a republic.

clue.text: Excited compiler: you earn invitation for the night

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so the words that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, worked up, propositions someone with a suggestive line about spending the night together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' looks like it describes the compiler's mood; it signals rearranging all the letters of COMPILER and YOU EARN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a familiar suggestive proposal asking whose home a couple should go back to for an overnight stay.

clue.text: Give new impetus to whistle-blower concerning silence

parts.note: a referee, REF, blows the whistle in a football match
RE is the formal word meaning about or concerning
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to revive a whistle-blower's story about something that was hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but here it is a sports official.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh something is to revive or invigorate it, giving it fresh energy.

clue.text: No longer with it perhaps, using broken sentences

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and the pieces reassembled, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone losing their faculties gives themselves away by speaking in fragmented sentences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SENTENCES; 'using' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent means growing old, and an ageing person may be thought out of touch, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Bachelor properly in cheerful mode

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
rightly means correctly or properly

explanation.surface: A single man, properly cheerful, as if pleased with his unattached life.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something brightly means doing it in a lively, sunny, upbeat manner.

clue.text: Dodgy banks covering a large part of Europe

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the shuffled bank letters go round the other pieces
dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Untrustworthy banks have spread their reach over much of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges BANKS, and 'covering' puts those shuffled letters around A plus L. 'a large' reads as one phrase in the surface but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkans is the peninsula region of south-eastern Europe, a sizeable portion of the continent.

clue.text: Urge on a naughty child, another one not following

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: not means the item named next is left out of the preceding word

parts.note: an elf is another mischievous sprite, like the imp
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone eggs on one mischievous child while another refuses to tag along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another one' points back to the naughty child: a second mischief-maker. 'not' tells you to drop the F that 'following' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward to act, which is to urge them on.

clue.text: Fish eggs exhausted oarsmen said to have enjoyed

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the phrase is matched by its pronunciation rather than its spelling

parts.note: rowers who are worn out have had a hard row, a gruelling spell at the oars

explanation.surface: A boat crew, worn out, refuel with a meal of fish roe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have enjoyed' is a link: exhausted oarsmen will have enjoyed (experienced) a hard row.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard roe is the egg mass of a female fish, as distinct from soft roe, the milt of a male.

clue.text: Discover diary not so full? Don't repeat that mistake

parts.note: to learn something is to discover or find it out
if your diary is not so full, there is less on for you: one's less on

explanation.surface: Someone checks a quieter calendar and resolves never to repeat the error that caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word splits as ONE'S LESS ON: a lighter diary means one has less on.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn one's lesson is to profit from a bad experience so that the same error is avoided.

clue.text: Flu panic disrupted a sporting event

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outbreak of influenza fear throws a big sporting fixture into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup final is the deciding match of a knockout competition, such as the FA Cup in English football.

clue.text: Desperately hard up in seclusion

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone badly short of money retreats from society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' looks like it intensifies 'hard up'; it rearranges HARD UP. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the practice of keeping women screened from public view, and more loosely any state of seclusion.

clue.text: In part of church they are on the phone, talking

indicators.note: talking means spoken aloud, so the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: apps are the programs installed on a smartphone

explanation.surface: Churchgoers chatting on their phones during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they are on the phone' looks like people making calls; it describes the software on a mobile, APPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded or vaulted recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Little picture hardly anyone looks at

definitions.note: read as 'what hardly anyone looks at', a noun phrase

parts.note: small means little
a print is a picture, such as a photograph or engraving

explanation.surface: A tiny artwork that gallery visitors walk straight past.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as 'what hardly anyone looks at'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine print of a contract holds terms that most people sign without ever reading.

clue.text: Potato that is providing iron

parts.note: mash is mashed potato
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A potato dish that supplies dietary iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like the mineral in food; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie is an old name for a golf club roughly equal to a modern five-iron.

clue.text: Charring and giving voice, full of energy

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the energy letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: singing is giving voice to a song
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone lively sings while burning the toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Singeing is lightly burning the surface of something, scorching it.

clue.text: Tony's project Hercules might not have welcomed?

definitions.meaning: Tony Blair's rebranding of the UK Labour Party in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A British prime minister's political scheme that a mythical hero would have resented.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony is Tony Blair, Labour Prime Minister of Britain 1997-2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair's modernised party was branded New Labour, and a fresh task is a new labour for Hercules.

clue.text: Couched again, relax with a little toy bear

parts.note: to rest is to relax
Ted is a short form of teddy, the toy bear

explanation.surface: A child relaxes on the sofa with a small teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couched' looks like lying on a couch; it means worded, as in couched in polite terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch something is to phrase it, so expressing it again in words is restating it.

clue.text: Circus artiste that can hold her drink?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed drinking glass, which holds a drink

explanation.surface: A circus acrobat who can drink without getting tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold her drink' suggests a woman's tolerance for alcohol; the glass literally holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an acrobat who tumbles and a straight-sided glass for drinks.

clue.text: Filth one suffers in prison

parts.note: dung is manure or filth

indicators.note: suffers suggests being knocked about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inmate endures squalor while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' rearranges ONE into EON; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell for holding prisoners, especially in a castle.

clue.text: Caribbean food is fairly extensive

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A judgement that Caribbean cuisine offers a broad range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Widish means somewhat wide, so moderately broad in extent.

clue.text: Removes old Scots in shows

parts.note: the prefix de- means remove, as in de-ice or de-bug
the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

explanation.surface: Something expels ancient Scottish tribes in a series of performances.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, to 'de-Pict' a place would be to remove its Picts.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to portray or represent something in a picture or words.

clue.text: As man, I pardon dreadfully histrionic woman

indicators.note: dreadfully means terribly, badly done, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man grudgingly forgives a theatrical woman for her tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link; the shuffled words are MAN I PARDON.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna, originally an opera's leading lady, now means any temperamental, self-dramatising person.

clue.text: Do out in full, as before

definitions.meaning: do is the written abbreviation of the word, so spelt out in full it is the answer
the word means the same again, as stated above

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry something out completely, just like last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb; it is the abbreviation do., written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say the same thing applies again, repeating what was stated earlier.

clue.text: A sound from chick, look!

definitions.meaning: the high cheep of a young bird
a quick look, here as an imperative

explanation.surface: Someone points out a baby bird chirping.
explanation.definitionFit: Peep is both a small bird's cry and a furtive glance.

clue.text: Grain: grind it, I say

indicators.note: I say signals speech, so the phrase is matched by its pronunciation

parts.note: to mill something is to grind it, so grind it becomes mill it

explanation.surface: An instruction to take some cereal and grind it into flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded cereal crop grown for food and birdseed.

clue.text: Minister's job can be dispiriting

parts.note: dispiriting reads as depressing, but it means driving out spirits, a clergyman's rite

explanation.surface: A clergyman's work can leave him feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispiriting' read as dis-spiriting: removing evil spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Expelling demons from a possessed person is a ritual performed by a priest or minister.

clue.text: Finally overcome resistance to dress in feathers?

parts.note: to wear is to dress in clothes
down is the soft fine feathers of birds

explanation.surface: Someone at last gives in and agrees to put on a feather costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear someone down is to erode their opposition by persistence until they give way.

clue.text: Object to being made to go again

definitions.meaning: to feel aggrieved at, to object to

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about being dispatched on an errand a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Resent means take offence at, while re-sent is the past participle of send again.
